title: Kyle — The Boonta Flats
source: four reference stills supplied by Kevin, kept in raw/; original film in that tradition
notes: Second version, built from scratch against Kevin's reference images rather than from v1. Three things are done differently from the start. The machine is engines-out-front towing a pod on cables, the silhouette the references establish, with the cables written bar-tight and in a single plane -- a trailing cable is the most reliable failure in this repo, so Kevin chose to keep them and QC hard. The pilot is written as a child in every shot he appears in, with the pod as a scale referent, because a generic 'pilot' rendered as an adult every time in v1. And both face shots are positive: a grin that reaches full width in the first second and then holds, which is the construction that survived 7.5 s in lindsey_sparky, after a review showed the last two films had drifted to uniformly grim expressions.

still.control: diptych: master on the left carries the design, scene master on the right

i2v.note: 249 frames always; trim after QC. Every clip gets a frame-by-frame check on the tow cables.

locks.subject: kyle_kx boy, a nine-year-old boy with child proportions, this exact face, short dark hair
locks.pilot: In the open pod sits kyle_kx boy, a small nine-year-old boy with child proportions, this exact face, wearing a battered open-face racing helmet with round goggles and a sand-coloured padded flight jerkin. He is unmistakably a small child in a machine built for someone far bigger: his head and shoulders barely clear the pod's cowling, the seat rises well above him, and the cockpit looks half empty around his small frame.
locks.racer: a home-built desert racer in two parts: two enormous scorched turbine engines running well out in front, side by side and slightly splayed, their wide dark intakes leading and long orange flame blasting backwards from the rear nozzles, and a small open pod trailing behind them carrying the pilot. The engines and the pod are joined by a pair of long steel tow cables that run straight and bar-tight under load, dead taut in a single plane with no slack, no loops and no loose ends, and a faint violet energy binder arcs between the two engines. Burnt copper and gunmetal panels, exposed ribbed casings and riveted plates. The whole machine hovers above the ground with open air beneath it and its shadow on the sand directly below; it has no wheels and nothing touches the ground
locks.flats: a vast flat ochre desert under a pale washed-out sky, low sandstone buttes strung along the far horizon, the ground a hard pale dust that lifts in sheets, heat shimmer flattening the distance
locks.staging: a crowded open staging ground outside a desert city, dozens of wildly different racing machines laid out in rows with their engines detached and lying on the sand, handlers and mechanics moving between them, pack animals and crates at the edges, a packed crowd behind a rope line in the foreground, fine dust hanging in the air over everything
locks.arena: a vast desert arena outside a sandstone city of great domed buildings, an enormous tiered stone grandstand packed solid with spectators running along one side, tall banners on poles, the open course of pale dust sweeping past it and out into the desert
locks.style: Cinematic film still from a late-1990s live-action science-fiction adventure, anamorphic 35mm on film stock, photoreal skin and scorched metal, hard high desert sun, slight haze and blown highlights, shallow depth of field, visible film grain, warm ochre and sand palette against a pale washed sky. Photorealistic, no cartoon or illustration styling, no text, no lettering, no logos, no watermark.
locks.pace: Everything moves at natural real-time speed, the full speed of a race, with no slow motion and no speed ramping.
